1. Open dolthub.com/repositories/post-no-preference/options and look at the two tables, `option_chain` and `volatility_history`.
2. Note the branch name. It is `master`, not `main`. Point the API at `main` and every query fails with branch not found, which is the single most common way people give up on this source.
3. Query it straight away at `https://www.dolthub.com/api/v1alpha1/post-no-preference/options/master?q= `. No key, no header, no account.
4. Only if you want the whole thing offline, install the `dolt` CLI and run `dolt clone post-no-preference/options`. After that a `dolt pull` brings each new day in. Expect tens of gigabytes.

This repository contains historical options data for three major U.S. equity ETFs: SPY (S&P 500), IWM (Russell 2000), and QQQ (Nasdaq-100). snippet:

14 years of End-of-Day SPY options data in parquet format
...
This dataset contains 14 years of raw, End-of-Day (EOD) options data for the SPY ETF, spanning from 2010 to 2023. The data represents the daily 4:00 PM EST closing snapshot of the options chain.

The original files were converted to .parquet format for fast loading and reduced memory usage. The data is completely unfiltered. No strikes or dates have been removed, and all original values (including empty fields) are preserved exactly as recorded.
